lead.headline: Private jet nose-dives onto Palm Beach County road, killing all 9 aboard
lead.dek: Pilot radioed a mayday as the Learjet fell 20,000 feet a minute; 600 evacuated from a mobile home park
body: A Learjet 60 carrying nine people nose-dived onto a roadway in a residential area of Palm Beach County, Florida, about 12:50 p.m. Sunday, killing everyone on board, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said. The jet had left Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas bound for North Eleuthera in the Bahamas, the FAA said.

Air traffic control recordings carried by LiveATC.net captured the pilot reporting light, clear ice and moderate turbulence at 35,000 feet and asking to climb 2,000 feet, then a mayday as the jet descended at 10,000 and then 20,000 feet per minute. "We're going to crash into the ground," the pilot said. Gov. Ron DeSantis said no one on the ground was reported hurt.

Palm Beach County evacuated about 600 residents of a mobile home park near the wreckage, County Commissioner Joel Flores said, and the sheriff's office closed Military Trail in both directions. The NTSB is investigating with FAA support. The jet is registered to a Delaware limited liability company, FAA records show; those aboard were not identified.

briefs.headline: Judge tosses DOJ suit to block Alaska Senate certification
briefs.summary: Judge Sharon Gleason ruled Sunday the Justice Department lacked standing to block certification if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses and had no workable plan to separate ballots for a second Daniel J. Sullivan. DOJ filed a notice of appeal.

briefs.headline: Sen. Chris Murphy hospitalized after stroke, office says
briefs.summary: The Connecticut Democrat, 53, felt numbness in his arm at his son's hockey game Saturday and was moved to Johns Hopkins for monitoring, chief of staff Allison Herwitt said Sunday. He is awake, alert and expected to recover fully, she said.

briefs.headline: Stevens endorses Republican Rogers; Schumer calls it a 'betrayal'
briefs.summary: Rep. Haley Stevens, who lost the August Democratic primary to Abdul El-Sayed, backed GOP nominee Mike Rogers on Sunday; Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, who had backed her, called it a "despicable betrayal."

briefs.headline: Judge throws out Trump's $10B suit against the Journal for good
briefs.summary: Judge Darrin Gayles in Miami dismissed the defamation case over the Epstein birthday letter with prejudice Saturday, writing that the amended complaint "falls short of pleading actual malice." He had let Trump refile after an April ruling.

briefs.headline: Trump says Iran war will end 'one way or the other' as Tehran holds reply
briefs.summary: Trump said Sunday that "either they'll make a deal, or we'll just end it," as Iranian negotiators spent a third day in Doha. Security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran has not answered a letter from Vice President JD Vance seeking talks.

briefs.headline: Iotova wins Bulgaria's presidential runoff with about 58%
briefs.summary: Acting President Iliana Iotova took 57.4% to 58.2% against Andrey Gyurov in Sunday's runoff, polling institutes estimated, and declared victory beside Prime Minister Rumen Radev. She would be the first elected woman president.

briefs.headline: Israel's election chief says results stand after Likud 'stolen' claim
briefs.summary: Central Elections Committee head Noam Sohlberg said Sunday the results would stand even if suspicions were substantiated, after Netanyahu's Likud said without evidence that Arab-led parties 'stole' the vote. The bloc holds 53 seats to 48.

briefs.headline: Hackers send false nuclear alerts through Ukraine's air raid app
briefs.summary: Ukraine's Air Force said the system was hacked late Sunday, sending false nuclear, chemical and street-fighting warnings cleared in about an hour. Russia's Emergencies Ministry said its own app was hit by a 'massive cyberattack' Monday.

briefs.headline: Voters decide 19 state Senate seats Tuesday, 18 of them contested
briefs.summary: Nineteen of the Senate's 34 seats are on Tuesday's ballot, with MetroNews rating two districts as possible Republican-to-Democrat flips, including Mike Oliverio's District 13, won last time by under 160 votes. Polls open 6:30 a.m.

briefs.headline: Citizenship voting amendment on every West Virginia ballot Tuesday
briefs.summary: The Citizenship Voting Requirement Amendment would write into the state constitution that only U.S. citizens may vote, a bar state law already imposes; it passed the Legislature unanimously in March and needs a simple majority.

briefs.headline: U.S. attorneys offer local police help on fraud investigations
briefs.summary: Moore Capito and Matt Harvey, the state's two U.S. attorneys, are meeting local and state police to take on fraud cases that short-staffed departments cannot, part of a national task force led by Vice President Vance.

briefs.headline: Mason County schools levy on ballot with $90M data center stake
briefs.summary: Mason County's school excess levy, renewed for 70-plus years at about $10 million a year, is on Tuesday's ballot; the Treasurer's Office says two data centers under construction could add $90 million if it passes, WSAZ reported Oct. 29.

regional.item: The Cabell County school board meets at 4:30 p.m. today, moved from Tuesday for Election Day, with 50,000 in flooring work on the agenda.
Two people were hospitalized with non-life-threatening stab wounds after an early Sunday confrontation on Kanawha Boulevard East; police seek a third person.
A driver fled a Parkersburg police stop near 19th Street and Murdoch Avenue Sunday afternoon and led a pursuit onto I-77 north at over 100 mph, dispatchers said.

away.item: Vermont is getting $60.3 million in federal money to replace 60 miles of rail between Rutland and North Bennington, VTDigger reported Oct. 27.

hotspots.item: Webster County's new school bus garage should reach substantial completion by Nov. 15, the school board heard Oct. 12, The Webster Echo reported Sunday.
Topsail Beach's Bush Marina is closed from today for the week for scheduled boat ramp maintenance, the town said in an Oct. 16 notice.

briefs.headline: Cougars end five-game skid with 5-4 win over Giants in Langley
briefs.summary: Tre Peck scored with 64 seconds left Sunday after Vancouver erased a 4-1 lead with three third-period goals. Kason Kobelka made 28 saves; Prince George, 4-7-0-2, opens a seven-game homestand Wednesday against Moose Jaw.

briefs.headline: Frizzell and new Prince George council take office Monday night
briefs.summary: Mayor-elect Garth Frizzell and the council elected last month take their oaths at Monday's inaugural meeting, which also receives the official results, sets the monthly acting-mayor rotation and names regional district appointees.

briefs.headline: Doerkson says he prefers B.C. public servants back in the office
briefs.summary: The premier-designate said Sunday some hybrid work will likely persist but his interest is in having staff return. BCGEU president Paul Finch said he was "a bit concerned," calling remote work a cost saver for the province.

briefs.headline: Carney calls six federal byelections for Dec. 7
briefs.summary: The votes fill seats in Ontario, Quebec and Saskatchewan left by MPs from all four parties, including Steven Guilbeault's Laurier-Sainte-Marie and Larry Brock's Brantford-Brant South, where a Brock-backed independent is also running.

briefs.headline: Trump says Canada-U.S. trade deal 'very close' after Carney call
briefs.summary: Carney wrote Sunday that the call built on talks over "the outlines of a mutually beneficial trade deal" and teams will work in the coming weeks. Trump told reporters in Iowa there is "the concept of a deal" with no tariffs on U.S. dairy.

briefs.headline: Five labs fail to replicate lasting psilocybin effects in mice
briefs.summary: Five labs at UC Berkeley, UCSF and Stanford ran identical psilocybin protocols in mice and found head twitching and acute anxiety but no lasting behavioral changes 24 hours after a dose, in Nature Neuroscience Monday.

briefs.headline: Mount Sinai trial pairs two tools to open calcified arteries wider
briefs.summary: In a 120-patient randomized trial, rotational atherectomy plus intravascular lithotripsy produced stents about 19% larger than lithotripsy alone in calcified nodules, Mount Sinai reported Sunday at the TCT conference. No deaths at 30 days.

briefs.headline: Cannabis use tied to 40% higher stroke odds in 442,906-adult survey
briefs.summary: Adults using cannabis one to five days a month had 23% higher odds of reported heart disease and 40% higher odds of stroke in a Tulane analysis of 442,906 survey responses, the American Heart Association said Monday. It is preliminary.

briefs.headline: 3D map finds 41% of nearby interstellar gas in unstable state
briefs.summary: A Technion team combined a Gaia dust map with an ultraviolet map to classify gas within about 4,000 light-years and found 27% cold, 32% warm and 41% unstable, against a 1969 two-state model. The analysis is under peer review.

briefs.headline: Vals AI scores 25 models on alignment with Beijing's positions
briefs.summary: Benchmark firm Vals AI asked 25 models hundreds of questions about China and found DeepSeek R1 most aligned with Beijing's positions and Grok 4.7 least, with Chinese-language prompts drawing more pro-government answers.

briefs.headline: India proposes sending AI models to data held in secure enclaves
briefs.summary: India's electronics ministry published a DEPA for AI Training framework under which hospitals, banks and agencies keep encrypted data in hardware-secured environments that models visit for training, with differential privacy and audit logs.

briefs.headline: Google says its Suncatcher satellite ran Gemma 4 inference in orbit
briefs.summary: Google said its experimental Suncatcher satellite, launched in early October, returned a haiku from an onboard Gemma 4 model on a TPU while passing over Svalbard. Google plans to test two linked satellites next year.

weather_ear: Monday's forecast arrives at 7:15 from Jim Claudtore's desk.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster and Summers-New River carry no regional line today; the Kyushu basho (tournament) opens Nov. 8 in Fukuoka, six days out.
